questions.q: Completa: Living with a host family was the best way to ___ my English.

task: Escribe 6 a 8 frases sobre las reglas de tu casa (o de un lugar donde viviste) usando had to / didn't have to.
paragraphs: When I arrived in Dublin to study English, I stayed with the Byrne family for two months. I was nervous before I met them, but they were very kind from the first day.
The Byrnes have two children, Ciara, who is ten, and Sean, who is fifteen. Mr Byrne works in a bank and Mrs Byrne is a vet. They live in a big old house with a garden, two cats and a lot of books.

There were a few rules in the house. I had to be home before eleven o'clock on weekdays, and I had to tell them if I wasn't coming home for dinner. I didn't have to cook or clean, but I usually helped with the washing-up.

At first, it was difficult to understand them because they spoke very fast and used a lot of Irish expressions. "What's the craic?" means "How are you?" or "What's happening?" After two or three weeks, it was much easier.

My favourite moments were the dinners. Every evening we sat together and talked about our day. Sean helped me with my homework and Ciara taught me some Irish songs. On my last night, they gave me a photo album with pictures of our time together.
I still write to them every month. Living with a host family was the best way to improve my English.
